punjab_cm_history.title: Our Chief Ministers
punjab_cm_history.publisher: Office of the Chief Minister, Punjab
punjab_cm_history.reviewed_excerpt: Official history lists Shahbaz Sharif, Hasan Askari Rizvi, Usman Buzdar, Hamza Shahbaz, Parvez Elahi, Mohsin Naqvi and Maryam Nawaz. Records retain oath-date and handover qualifications.

elahi_oath.title: President administers oath to Parvez Elahi
elahi_oath.publisher: Press Information Department, Government of Pakistan
elahi_oath.reviewed_excerpt: The Presidency records the chief minister oath on 27 July 2022. The CM history lists 26 July; this register uses the oath event and retains the discrepancy.

naqvi_oath.title: Mohsin Naqvi takes oath as caretaker Punjab CM
naqvi_oath.reviewed_excerpt: The Monday 23 January article reports the oath occurred Sunday night, 22 January. This matches the official CM history. Publication date is not used as the oath date.

caretaker_portfolios.title: Caretaker Punjab portfolios assigned
caretaker_portfolios.reviewed_excerpt: Javaid Akram is named for Specialized Healthcare, Jamal Nasir for Primary and Secondary Healthcare, and Mansoor Qadir for Higher and School Education. Ministers took oath the preceding day. Exact portfolio notification and end dates still need review.

pages.text:
CHAPTER 13
DISTRICT HEALTH AUTHORITY ATTOCK
13.1 Introduction
There are 24 formations in DHA Attock out of which audit of 05
formations was conducted. Total expenditure and receipt of these
formations was Rs 4268.574 and Rs 60.168 million respectively out of

CHAPTER 8
DISTRICT HEALTH AUTHORITY KASUR
8.1 Introduction
There are 26 formations in District Health Authority (DHA), Kasur
out of which audit of 05 formations was conducted. Total expenditure and
receipt of DHA Kasur was Rs 3,548.894 million and Rs 36.249 million
respectively out of which 45.7% of expenditure and 37.8% of receipts
were audited.
a) Audit Profile of DHA Kasur
Rs in million
Sr. Total Formations Expenditure Receipt
Description
No. Formations Audited Audited Audited
1 DHA Kasur 26 05 1623.996 13.718
b) Comments on Budget and Accounts (Variance Analysis)
As per appropriation accounts, original budget of DHA Kasur was
Rs 5,801.858 million and supplementary grant was Rs 316.573 million for
the FY 2023-24. An amount of Rs 1,352.941 million was surrendered and
final budget was Rs 4,765.491 million. Management incurred an
expenditure of Rs 3,548.894 million resulting in saving of Rs 1,216.596
million. Actual expenditure was less than the original budget which
indicated that unrealistic budget estimates were made while demanding
the supplementary grant. The break-up is given below:

The above table also shows the development expenditure and number of
development schemes executed during FY 2022-23 and FY 2023-24. The total
development expenditure increased by 55% i.e. from Rs 519.568 million to
Rs 1,460.040 million in FY 2023-24. The major decrease was seen in DHAs
Sahiwal, Bahawalpur and Bahawalnagar. However, in DHA Faisalabad, Multan
and Jhang development expenditure increased from Rs 27.319 million to
Rs 703.387 million.
The data presented in the above tables indicates serious inadequacies in
the initial planning and resource allocation. The discrepancies underscore the
necessity for an in-depth analysis of the planning process within DHAs. Identifying
and understanding inconsistencies in the planning phase is crucial for enhancing
the effectiveness of future development initiatives.

CHAPTER 19
DISTRICT HEALTH AUTHORITY MIANWALI
19.1 Introduction
There are 22 formations in DHA Mianwali out of which audit of
05 formations was conducted. Total expenditure and receipt of these
formations was Rs 511.652 million and Rs 94.603 million respectively,
out of which 28% expenditure & 17% receipt was audited.
a) Audit Profile of DHA, Mianwali

b) Comments on Budget and Accounts (Variance Analysis)
As per appropriation accounts for the FY 2023-24 of the DHA,
Mianwali, original budget (development and non-development) was Rs
4,285.567 million, supplementary grant was Rs 390.153 million and
amount surrendered was Rs 1,560.775 million. The final budget was Rs
3,114.945 million. Against the final budget, expenditure of Rs 2,817.850
million was incurred resulting in saving of Rs 297.095 million. The break-
up of total budget and expenditure is given in the following table:

development schemes executed during FY 2022-23 and FY 2023-24. The total
development expenditure increased by 55% i.e. from Rs 519.568 million to
Rs 1,460.040 million in FY 2023-24. The major decrease was seen in DHAs

and Jhang development expenditure increased from Rs 27.319 million to
Rs 703.387 million.

the initial planning and resource allocation. The discrepancies underscore the
necessity for an in-depth analysis of the planning process within DHAs. Identifying
and understanding inconsistencies in the planning phase is crucial for enhancing
the effectiveness of future development initiatives.

CHAPTER 6
DISTRICT HEALTH AUTHORITY NAROWAL
6.1 Introduction
There are 17 formations in DHA Narowal out of which audit of 05
formations was conducted. Total expenditure and receipt of these
formations was Rs 3,259.704 and Rs 71.298 million respectively out of
which 71.83% expenditure and 47% receipt were audited.

b) Comments on Budget and Accounts (Variance Analysis)
As per appropriation accounts, original budget of DHA Narowal
was Rs 4,113.099 million and supplementary grant was Rs 825.178
million for the FY 2023-24. An amount of Rs 1,047.163 million was
surrendered and final budget was Rs 3,892.114 million. Management
incurred an expenditure of Rs 3,259.704 million resulting in saving of
Rs 632.410 million. Actual expenditure was less than the original budget
which indicated that unrealistic budget estimates were made while
demanding the supplementary grant. The break-up of final grant and

The above table also shows the development expenditure and number of
development schemes executed during FY 2022-23 and FY 2023-24. The total
development expenditure increased by 55% i.e. from Rs 519.568 million to
Rs 1,460.040 million in FY 2023-24. The major decrease was seen in DHAs
Sahiwal, Bahawalpur and Bahawalnagar. However, in DHA Faisalabad, Multan
and Jhang development expenditure increased from Rs 27.319 million to
Rs 703.387 million.
The data presented in the above tables indicates serious inadequacies in
the initial planning and resource allocation. The discrepancies underscore the
necessity for an in-depth analysis of the planning process within DHAs. Identifying
and understanding inconsistencies in the planning phase is crucial for enhancing
the effectiveness of future development initiatives.

As per appropriation accounts, original budget of DHA
Sheikhupura was Rs 6,418.806 million and supplementary grant was Rs
4.044 million for the FY 2023-24. An amount of Rs 301.154 million was
surrendered and final budget was Rs 6,121.310 million. Management
incurred an expenditure of Rs 5,165.998 million resulting in saving of Rs

7.1 Introduction
a) There are 19 formations in DHA Sialkot out of which audit of 07

out of which 54% expenditure and 67% receipt were audited.

b) Comments on Budget and Accounts (Variance Analysis)
As per appropriation accounts, original budget of DHA Sialkot was
Rs 3,789.026 million and supplementary grant was Rs 1,408.457 million
for the FY 2023-24. An amount of Rs 968.457million was surrendered and
final budget was Rs 4,228.026 million. Management incurred an
expenditure of Rs 3,994.044 million resulting in saving of Rs
233.99million. Actual expenditure was less than the original budget which
indicated that unrealistic budget estimates were made while demanding
the supplementary grant. The break-up of final grant and expenditure is

The above table also shows the development expenditure and number of
development schemes executed during FY 2022-23 and FY 2023-24. The total
development expenditure increased by 55% i.e. from Rs 519.568 million to
Rs 1,460.040 million in FY 2023-24. The major decrease was seen in DHAs
Sahiwal, Bahawalpur and Bahawalnagar. However, in DHA Faisalabad, Multan
and Jhang development expenditure increased from Rs 27.319 million to
Rs 703.387 million.
The data presented in the above tables indicates serious inadequacies in
the initial planning and resource allocation. The discrepancies underscore the
necessity for an in-depth analysis of the planning process within DHAs. Identifying
and understanding inconsistencies in the planning phase is crucial for enhancing
the effectiveness of future development initiatives.

ev-ed53237a3a6a121f37cf.title: GPIS Punjab-wide methodology
ev-ed53237a3a6a121f37cf.text: Education is the mean of total literacy, female literacy, and 100 minus the male-female literacy gap, from Census 2023.

ev-58dd811a36f1b184d4b3.title: GPIS Punjab-wide methodology
ev-58dd811a36f1b184d4b3.text: Health counts hospitals, dispensaries, RHCs and BHUs in PHS Table 3 as at 31 December 2023, divides by Census 2023 population per 100,000, and min-max normalizes across all 36 census districts. It measures reported capacity, not quality or outcomes.

ev-2bc60b3d516ec3dd5064.title: GPIS Punjab-wide methodology
ev-2bc60b3d516ec3dd5064.text: Accountability averages total and development DHA expenditure divided by final grant for FY 2023-24. Each contribution is bounded to 0–100; raw utilization and source discrepancies remain visible. Utilization is not proof of integrity or impact.

ev-57f4a243927f488a4f5b.title: GPIS Punjab-wide methodology
ev-57f4a243927f488a4f5b.text: Overall is the equal-weight mean of the rounded education, health and accountability scores under punjab-v1. It combines Census 2023, health capacity at 31 December 2023 and FY 2023-24 DHA budgets, not an annual outcome or a politician rating.

ev-6de9df8a14da7e1dad8f.text: Reviewed source register entry. Open the official source for the original document.

ev-18f9211aa687b850373f.title: GPIS Prototype Methodology and RAG Architecture
ev-18f9211aa687b850373f.text: The education score is the arithmetic mean of total literacy percentage, female literacy percentage, and gender parity, where gender parity equals 100 minus the absolute male-female literacy gap. The score is rounded to one decimal.

ev-edc7b42d84410631620e.title: GPIS Prototype Methodology and RAG Architecture
ev-edc7b42d84410631620e.text: The health score counts listed public facilities, divides by population to obtain facilities per 100,000 residents, and min-max normalizes that rate from 0 to 100 within the fixed ten-district cohort. It measures relative listed facility availability, not quality or health outcomes.

ev-202c6fbcedaba59d6cd3.title: GPIS Prototype Methodology and RAG Architecture
ev-202c6fbcedaba59d6cd3.text: The accountability score is the arithmetic mean of overall budget utilization and development-budget utilization. Each utilization is 100 minus its reported lapse percentage. It is a financial-utilization proxy and is not proof of honesty, corruption, service quality, or impact.

ev-31b8bd83f2fae89dc3ef.title: GPIS Prototype Methodology and RAG Architecture
ev-31b8bd83f2fae89dc3ef.text: The overall GPIS score is the equal-weight arithmetic mean of the education, health, and accountability scores, rounded to one decimal. A high overall score only summarizes the selected indicators and their current definitions.

ev-846436a6aaf4b130ca90.title: GPIS Prototype Methodology and RAG Architecture
ev-846436a6aaf4b130ca90.text: The only supported year-over-year metric is development-budget utilization, calculated as expenditure divided by final grant times 100 for FY 2022-23 and FY 2023-24. The change is current utilization minus previous utilization in percentage points; it is not a change in the full accountability or overall score.

3.1 Introduction
a) There are 27 formations in DHA Gujrat out of which audit of 07
formations was conducted. Total expenditure and receipt of these
formations was Rs 1,882.794 and Rs 17.312 million respectively out of
which 53% expenditure and 67% receipt were audited.

b) Comments on Budget and Accounts (Variance Analysis)
As per appropriation accounts, original budget of DHA Gujrat was
Rs 3,715.830 million and supplementary grant was Rs 541.592 million for
the FY 2023-24. An amount of Rs 634.905 million was surrendered and
final budget was Rs 3,622.518 million. Management incurred an
expenditure of Rs 3,578.426 million resulting in saving of Rs 44.091
million. In case of development, actual expenditure was less than the
original budget which indicated that unrealistic budget estimates were
made while demanding the supplementary grant. The break-up of final
grant and expenditure is given in the following table:

a) There are 13 formations in DHA Hafizabad out of which audit of

b) Comments on Budget and Accounts (Variance Analysis)
As per appropriation accounts ,original budget of DHA Hafizabad
was Rs 2,295.481 million and supplementary grant was Rs 264.357
million for the FY 2023-24. An amount of Rs 341.994 million was
surrendered and final budget was Rs 2,217.844 million. Management
incurred an expenditure of Rs 1,965.358 million resulting in saving of Rs
252.486 million. Actual expenditure was less than the original budget
which indicated unrealistic budget estimates were made while demanding
the supplementary grant. The break-up of final grant and expenditure is
given in the following table:

final budget was Rs 4,765.491 million. Management incurred an
expenditure of Rs 3,548.894 million resulting in saving of Rs 1,216.596
million. Actual expenditure was less than the original budget which

which 37.74% expenditure and 22 % receipt were audited.

b) Comments on Budget and Accounts (Variance Analysis)
As per appropriation accounts, original budget of DHA Mandi
Bahauddin was Rs 4323.989 million and supplementary grant was Rs
419.730 million for the FY 2023-24. An amount of Rs 220.114 million
was surrendered and final budget was Rs 4,523.605 million. Management
incurred an expenditure of Rs 2,443.130 million resulting in saving of
Rs2,080.474 million. Actual expenditure was less than the original budget
which indicated that unrealistic budget estimates were made while
demanding the supplementary grant. The break-up of final grant and
expenditure is given in the following table:

development expenditure increased by 55% i.e. from Rs 519.568 million to

the initial planning and resource allocation. The discrepancies underscore the
necessity for an in-depth analysis of the planning process within DHAs. Identifying
and understanding inconsistencies in the planning phase is crucial for enhancing
the effectiveness of future development initiatives.

ev-b1b749d66d517199de09.title: Our Chief Ministers
ev-b1b749d66d517199de09.publisher: Office of the Chief Minister, Punjab
ev-b1b749d66d517199de09.text: Official history lists Shahbaz Sharif, Hasan Askari Rizvi, Usman Buzdar, Hamza Shahbaz, Parvez Elahi, Mohsin Naqvi and Maryam Nawaz. Records retain oath-date and handover qualifications.

ev-d98c9634bda830b26ffb.title: President administers oath to Parvez Elahi
ev-d98c9634bda830b26ffb.publisher: Press Information Department, Government of Pakistan
ev-d98c9634bda830b26ffb.text: The Presidency records the chief minister oath on 27 July 2022. The CM history lists 26 July; this register uses the oath event and retains the discrepancy.

ev-7e00ff602befce225054.title: Mohsin Naqvi takes oath as caretaker Punjab CM
ev-7e00ff602befce225054.text: The Monday 23 January article reports the oath occurred Sunday night, 22 January. This matches the official CM history. Publication date is not used as the oath date.

ev-b29b2569bc51a5b09749.title: Caretaker Punjab portfolios assigned
ev-b29b2569bc51a5b09749.text: Javaid Akram is named for Specialized Healthcare, Jamal Nasir for Primary and Secondary Healthcare, and Mansoor Qadir for Higher and School Education. Ministers took oath the preceding day. Exact portfolio notification and end dates still need review.
